newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin says April revenue up 16 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin says April revenue up 16 pct yr/yr.

text.p: April revenues for the Czech state budget grew 16 percent year-on-year, suggesting eight percent revenue growth for the whole year was achievable, Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik told parliament on Wednesday.
"I believe that the pace of eight percent (growth in revenues)...will be achieved," Kocarnik said in a debate on the state of the economy.

He said new data showed a recovery from lower-than-expected first quarter revenue growth which forced the government to make 25.5 billion crowns in expenditure cuts aimed at bringing the budget back into balance by the end of the year.
The 1997 budget, which was originally approved as balanced with forecast revenue and expenditure of 549 billion crowns, showed a 12 billion crown deficit at the end of April.
From January to date, revenue growth accelerated to 5.5 percent year-on-year from 4.7 percent for the first four months of the year.
Kocarnik added that "April data on the development of the economy will be positive".
